lead: Milwaukee plumbing deals with deep cold, old duplexes, basements and a large number of lead service lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Milwaukee.
risk: lead service lines, frozen pipes and basement backups
risk_short: lead lines, frozen pipes and basement backups
why: Milwaukee has tens of thousands of homes built before 1951 with lead service lines, plus galvanized supply pipes and cast-iron stacks. Polish flats and duplexes in Bay View and Riverwest are common.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and can freeze service lines. Heavy storms back up sewers into basements in older neighborhoods.
water: Milwaukee Water Works treats water from Lake Michigan. It is moderately hard. The utility is replacing lead service lines and has an address lookup.
tips: Check Milwaukee Water Works' lead line lookup.
Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Know where each unit's shutoff is in a duplex.
areas: PipeMend works in Bay View, Riverwest, the East Side, Walker's Point, Washington Heights, Sherman Park, the Third Ward and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Milwaukee Department of Neighborhood Services, and plumbers must be licensed by the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services.

faq.q: Does my Milwaukee home have a lead water line?
faq.a: If it was built before 1951, it may. Milwaukee has one of the largest numbers of lead service lines in the country. Milwaukee Water Works has an address lookup and a replacement program.
